body: Looks like other online validators report the same issue too (see, for example, http://www.utilities-online.info/xsdvalidation/#.VqAFvvH1GRs). Can we replace `xsd:sequence` with something else that doesn't require a certain order of the elements being used so that we remove one of the two lines?

``` xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<xsd:schema xmlns="http://symfony.com/schema/dic/services"
     xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
     targetNamespace="http://symfony.com/schema/dic/services"
     elementFormDefault="qualified">

  <!-- ... -->

  <xsd:element name="container" type="container" />

  <xsd:complexType name="container">
    <xsd:annotation>
      <xsd:documentation><![CDATA[
        The root element of a service file.
      ]]></xsd:documentation>
    </xsd:annotation>
    <xsd:choice maxOccurs="unbounded">
      <xsd:element name="imports" type="imports" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1" />
      <xsd:element name="parameters" type="parameters" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1" />
      <xsd:element name="services" type="services" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1" />
      <xsd:any namespace="##other" processContents="lax" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded" />
    </xsd:choice>
  </xsd:complexType>

  <!-- ... -->
</xsd:schema>
```

What about something like this?

@xabbuh That would probably do it. It does lose the order in which the child elements can appear and that may be important in some edge cases that I'm not aware of.

I'm seriously wondering if this is some sort of merge bug introduced when the definition was updated for a recent release.  I never had it before in quite a few years of using Symfony DIC as a standalone component.  Just a thought.  Unfortunately as the file is not versioned (it's been -1.0 for years,) it's hard to tell.

This part didn't change in years indeed. So I guess it has always been invalid but working.

This SO question resembles ours pretty well: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/25178259/xsd-allow-elements-from-different-namespace-anywhere-in-a-sequence
If PHP supports XSD 1.1 we could use the open content model.

And with XSD 1.1 we could also use "conditional type assignment" to do some conditional attributes, e.g. as with #17323

I can't see PHP utilising latest XML based technologies any time soon.  Been waiting for years for it to catch up - any time I need to do some serious XML stuff I off load it to something that can handle it.

So, can we just fix the existing XSD.  I'd be happy to do it if someone could point me at the right place to get code and test cases.
@chippyash do you think that this could be solved with the new XSD showed by @xabbuh? In case it is, this issue will be easy to solve. Thanks!

@xabbuh's XSD wont work as one could provide multiple `imports`-elements (because he can repeat the choice to add one or zero imports)

what would work is this: (edit: **NO IT DOESNT!!! look my next comment**)

according to https://github.com/symfony/symfony/issues/11266 the file at http://symfony.com/schema/dic/services/services-1.0.xsd gets updated then ;)

@backbone87 you are right. We just need someone to make a pull request changing this file: https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/2.3/src/Symfony/Component/DependencyInjection/Loader/schema/dic/services/services-1.0.xsd  As always, create the PR for the oldest maintained branch where this error should be fixed. This is probably the 2.3 branch, but I'm not sure.

Then, we'll merge the PR and symfony.com will publish the new version in a few minutes. Thanks!
